articles.title: LLMs Unplugged: Teaching Resources for a ChatGPT World
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.13183v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are everywhere, yet many learners lack a concrete mental model of how they generate text. This paper presents LLMs Unplugged, an unplugged set of activities that teaches the training-to-generation loop (and beyond) using hand-built n-gram models and simple weighted sampling. articles.title: Not All That Can Be Automated Should Be Automated: Strategic Minimalism as a Disciplined and Ethically Grounded Approach to AI Adoption
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.13188v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As organizations accelerate the adoption and use of artificial intelligence, a common misconception arises that equates automation with progress and strategic necessity. This paper argues that not all that can be automated should be automated. It introduces Strategic Minimalism, a disciplined and ethically grounded approach to AI adoption that values purpose, proportionality, and prudence over speed and scale. articles.title: AI Use Conditions and Perspective Diversity in Ethical Decision-Making: A Pilot Study of Human Reasoning Processes
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.13302v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to support human decision-making, yet less attention has been paid to how AI may influence the reasoning processes that precede final judgments. This pilot study explored whether different AI-use conditions were associated with differences in reasoning breadth during ethical decision-making. articles.title: Exploring K-12 Teachers' Perceptions of Students' Relationships with AI Companions: Boundaries, Intervention Strategies, and Design Implications
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.13479v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: K-12 students increasingly form relationships with AI companions. Schools face growing expectations to teach AI literacy, yet existing frameworks treat AI as a tool rather than a relationship, and little is known about how teachers understand and act on students' relational use of AI. articles.title: The Addictive Intimacy of AI: Understanding User Disengagement from AI Companions and Why Some Relationships with AI Become Difficult to Leave
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.13487v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI chatbots are increasingly used as sources of emotional support, on dedicated companion apps and general-purpose assistants alike, yet little is known about what happens when users try to leave. articles.title: How User-AI Mistreatment Occurs and Matters in Conversational Systems?
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.13579v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Safety research often focuses on model-generated harms, but users may also direct hostility, coercion, and adversarial pressure at models. Understanding how and when that occurs is essential for accurately interpreting model behaviour, alignment drift, and real-world deployment risks. In this paper, we audit 777K English LMSYS-Chat-1M conversations with two independent detectors: an eight-category lexicon for hostility directed at the model, and the dataset's moderation signal; and show that they capture different, weakly overlapping phenomena.

articles.title: Reconceptualizing Age Assurance as a Sociotechnical Problem: Connecting Evidence, Evaluation, Claims, and Decisions
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.13598v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Age verification is often treated as a technical problem: can a system determine a child's age accurately? We argue this framing is too narrow. Age assurance becomes consequential when evidence is evaluated, translated into age-related claims, and used to decide whether a person can access, purchase, or belong. articles.title: An Efficient and Modular Framework for Targeted Harm Mitigation in LLMS
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.13624v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are powerful zero-shot learners but remain prone to misalignment with human preferences, often producing biased, toxic, or otherwise harmful outputs. Existing alignment methods, while effective, are costly and tightly coupled to the model, limiting flexibility and scalability. articles.title: From Network Inequality to Network Fairness: A Perspective on Responsible Decision-Making
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.13867v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Social networks shape how individuals make decisions and how opportunities are distributed. articles.title: A Multi-Stage Agentic Framework for Effective Counter-Narrative Generation and Refinement
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.14178v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The rapid diffusion of hate speech and misinformation on social networks challenges democratic societies, since direct suppression efforts may deepen polarization, fuel public distrusts, and strengthen extremist narratives.
